title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit
lede: Satya Nadella told the DealBook Summit that Microsoft's October buyout offer to 60,000 staff was about reorganizing work around AI rather than replacing people, and about giving employees a choice.

points: Nadella says the aim is a company where everyone works through AI and jobs shift toward directing it.
He framed the buyout, instead of another mass layoff, as a way for staff to feel they had agency.
His example is the Cowork team in Microsoft 365: 11 developers who build a software factory, which in turn builds the product.
He expects every job to become managing agents, and says an incumbent of Microsoft's age will take longer to change than people expect.
On a podcast, he blamed singularity talk and job-loss predictions for leaving workers anxious about their future.

sections.text: Nadella's view is that software engineering survives but reorganizes around agents, so developers should expect the job to tilt toward specifying and supervising AI output.
